statement: If a straight line be bisected and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the rectangle contained by the whole with the added straight line and the added straight line together with the square on the half is equal to the square on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line.
heath_proof: For let a straight line AB be bisected at the point C, and let a straight line BD be added to it in a straight line;  I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD. For let the square CEFD be described on CD, [I. 46] and let DE be joined; through the point B let BG be drawn parallel to either EC or DF, through the point H let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF, and further through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or DM. [I. 31] Then, since AC is equal to CB, AL is also equal to CH. [I. 36]But CH is equal to HF. [I. 43] Therefore AL is also equal to HF. Let CM be added to each; therefore the whole AM is equal to the gnomon NOP. But AM is the rectangle AD, DB, for DM is equal to DB; therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB. Let LG, which is equal to the square on BC, be added to each; therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the gnomon NOP and LG. But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFD, which is described on CD; therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD.
ai_proof_text:
2.6
**Statement:** If a straight line be bisected and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the rectangle contained by the whole with the added straight line and the added straight line together with the square on the half is equal to the square on the straight line made up of the half and the added straight line.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line AB be bisected at C, so that AC = CB, and let the straight line BD be added to it in a straight line, so that A, C, B, D lie in this order on the single straight line AD. It is required to prove that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD.

**Step 2.** On CD describe the square CEFD [1.46], CE and DF being the sides drawn at right angles to CD and EF the side opposite to CD, and join DE [P1]. By its construction in 1.46 the square has its opposite sides parallel, CE ∥ DF and CD ∥ EF, so CEFD is a parallelogram with DE as a diameter; and all its sides are equal and all its angles are right [D1.22].

**Step 3.** Through B draw BG parallel to CE [1.31], meeting the diameter DE at H and the side EF at G; through H draw KM parallel to AD [1.31], meeting CE at L and DF at M; and through A draw AK parallel to DM [1.31], meeting KM at K.

**Step 4.** Since BG ∥ CE and CE ∥ DF, also BG ∥ DF; since AK ∥ DM and DM ∥ CE, also AK ∥ CE; and since KM ∥ AD and AD ∥ EF, also KM ∥ EF [1.30]. Hence each of the figures AL (= AKLC), CH (= CLHB), BM (= BHMD), LG (= LEGH), HF (= HGFM), CM (= CLMD) and AM (= AKMD) has its opposite sides parallel and is a parallelogram. Because H lies on the diameter DE, LG and BM are the parallelograms about the diameter DE of the parallelogram CEFD, and CH, HF are their complements; the parallelogram BM together with the two complements CH, HF is a gnomon [D2.2], which we call the gnomon NOP. The gnomon NOP together with LG makes up the whole square CEFD.

**Step 5.** Since AC = CB, the parallelograms AL and CH are on the equal bases AC, CB and in the same parallels AD, KM; therefore AL = CH [1.36].

**Step 6.** Since CH and HF are the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter DE of the parallelogram CEFD, CH = HF [1.43].

**Step 7.** Therefore AL = HF [CN1].

**Step 8.** Let CM be added to each. AL together with CM is the whole parallelogram AM, and HF together with CM (which is made up of CH and BM) is the gnomon NOP. Therefore AM = gnomon NOP [CN2].

**Step 9.** Now BM is a parallelogram about the diameter of the square CEFD; hence BM is itself a square [2.4, Porism], so that DM = DB [D1.22]. Further, AM is a parallelogram whose angle ADM is the angle CDF of the square and is therefore right [D1.22]; since AK ∥ DM and AD falls on them, the angle KAD together with the angle ADM equals two right angles [1.29], so KAD is right; and the angles AKM, KMD, being opposite to ADM, KAD in the parallelogram AM, are also right [1.34]. Thus AM is a rectangular parallelogram, namely the rectangle contained by AD, DM [D2.1]; and since DM = DB, AM is the rectangle contained by AD, DB.

**Step 10.** Therefore the gnomon NOP is equal to the rectangle contained by AD, DB [CN1].

**Step 11.** Again, LG is a parallelogram about the diameter of the square CEFD, so LG is a square [2.4, Porism]; and its side LH is equal to CB, these being opposite sides of the parallelogram CH [1.34]. Therefore LG is the square on a straight line equal to CB, that is, LG is equal to the square on CB.

**Step 12.** Let LG be added to each. Then the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the gnomon NOP together with LG [CN2]. But the gnomon NOP together with LG is the whole square CEFD, which is the square described on CD. Therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD [CN1]. Q.E.D.

Path note: For DM = DB and for LG being a square, the most direct route is the Porism to 2.4 (in a square the parallelograms about the diameter are squares); the same facts could be derived at greater length from the angle theorems of Book 1 alone, but that longer route was not taken.
